question: What is the primary purpose of a living will within the context of the Living Will Movement?

options.A: To distribute a patient's financial assets after death
options.B: To document specific medical treatment preferences for end-of-life care
options.C: To grant a family member full ownership of patient medical records
options.D: To allow physicians to make unilateral decisions without family input

explanation: A living will is an advance directive specifically designed to allow individuals to document their medical treatment preferences before losing the capacity to do so. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h1)

question: Why did the Living Will Movement emerge alongside advancements in medical technology?

options.A: Technology made it easier to cure all terminal illnesses completely
options.B: Machines created situations where biological life could be artificially prolonged indefinitely
options.C: Hospitals required legal protection against high financial costs
options.D: Patients demanded that all available machines be used in every situation

explanation: The movement arose because modern technology made it possible to artificially prolong life, forcing society to address whether such interventions are always beneficial. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h1)

question: Who first proposed the concept of a living will in 1967?
explanation: Attorney Luis Kutner is credited with first proposing the concept of the living will in 1967 as a legal instrument for end-of-life choices. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h2)

question: What was the significance of the 1990 Patient Self-Determination Act (PSDA)?

options.A: It forced all citizens to draft a living will before turning 65
options.B: It mandated that federally funded healthcare facilities inform patients of their right to execute advance directives
options.C: It made euthanasia legal across all healthcare institutions
options.D: It gave physicians complete authority to override family wishes

explanation: The PSDA required healthcare facilities to provide adult patients with information regarding their rights to make advance directives upon admission. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h2)

question: How does a living will primarily differ from a durable power of attorney for healthcare?

options.A: A living will designates a person to make decisions, while a DPOA lists specific treatments
options.B: A living will provides written instructions for specific treatments, whereas a DPOA designates a surrogate decision-maker
options.C: A living will is only valid for financial matters, while a DPOA is strictly for medical care
options.D: A living will can be changed by the family, while a DPOA can only be changed by a judge

explanation: A living will contains instructional guidelines regarding treatments, while a DPOA-HC appoints a proxy to make dynamic decisions for the patient. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h3)

question: In clinical practice, why might a healthcare proxy be needed even if a patient has a living will?

options.A: To pay the remaining hospital bills out of pocket
options.B: To interpret patient values and make real-time decisions for unforeseen clinical situations
options.C: To legally override the explicit written wishes in the living will
options.D: To perform surgical procedures if the physician is unavailable

explanation: A healthcare proxy is vital because a written living will cannot possibly anticipate every unique clinical scenario that may arise during a crisis. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h3)

question: Which ethical principle provides the primary justification for honoring a living will?
explanation: Autonomy is the principle of self-determination, affirming that competent patients have the right to decide their own medical treatment path. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h4)

question: What is the primary ethical conflict a nurse may face when managing an end-of-life patient with a living will?

options.A: Balancing the cost of hospital equipment against insurance coverage
options.B: Balancing the duty to preserve life against the obligation to respect a peaceful, natural death
options.C: Deciding which family member receives financial inheritance
options.D: Determining whether the physician holds a valid medical license

explanation: Nurses often struggle with the traditional goal of preserving life versus the ethical duty to honor a patient's choice to refuse burdensome, life-prolonging treatments. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h4)

question: How does a living will relate to the concept of informed consent?

options.A: It allows a patient to give prospective consent or refusal for medical treatments before losing capacity
options.B: It replaces the need for any physician explanation of surgical risks
options.C: It is a financial contract rather than a medical document
options.D: It transfers all legal liability from the hospital to the patient's employer

explanation: A living will acts as a tool for prospective informed consent, allowing individuals to consent to or refuse treatments before incapacitation occurs. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h5)

question: Why is it important for nurses to provide accurate, unbiased education regarding procedures like CPR during end-of-life planning?

options.A: To convince every patient to sign a do-not-resuscitate order immediately
options.B: To ensure patients understand the realities and outcomes of interventions, supporting true autonomous choice
options.C: To reduce the financial liability of the nursing staff in malpractice suits
options.D: To comply with hospital administrative quotas for advance directives

explanation: Accurate education ensures that patients understand the true outcomes of interventions, which is essential for making genuinely informed choices. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h5)

question: What is a common clinical problem associated with phrasing in living wills like 'no heroic measures'?

options.A: It is legally invalid in all court systems globally
options.B: It is vague and open to multiple interpretations by clinicians and families
options.C: It automatically grants financial power of attorney to the attending physician
options.D: It forces hospitals to discharge the patient immediately

explanation: Vague terms like 'heroic measures' lack specific clinical clarity, leading to confusion and conflict among healthcare providers and family members during a crisis. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h6)

question: How do cultural and religious beliefs often act as a barrier to advance care planning?

options.A: They mandate that living wills be notarized by religious leaders
options.B: They can create taboos around discussing death, making families reluctant to initiate advance planning
options.C: They legally prohibit hospitals from accepting advance directives
options.D: They require all patients to undergo life support regardless of diagnosis

explanation: In many cultures, discussing death is avoided or considered taboo, which creates a significant barrier to having open conversations about advance directives. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h6)

question: What is one of the primary responsibilities of a nurse in advocating for advance directives?

options.A: Drafting legal documents independently without consulting the patient
options.B: Educating patients and facilitating conversations about their values and end-of-life wishes
options.C: Overriding family wishes to implement personal clinical preferences
options.D: Filing court petitions to enforce living wills automatically

explanation: Nurses serve as key educators and facilitators, helping patients explore their values and document their wishes appropriately. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h7)

question: How should a nurse respond when family members demand aggressive life support that directly contradicts a patient's valid living will?

options.A: Comply immediately with the family to avoid emotional conflict
options.B: Act as a patient advocate by mediating discussions and upholding the documented wishes of the patient
options.C: Discharge the patient immediately from the healthcare facility
options.D: Ignore both documents and follow hospital routine protocol

explanation: The nurse must advocate for the patient by ensuring their documented autonomous wishes take precedence, while supporting and mediating with the family. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h7)
